properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 5 at 9:12AM EDT until September 5 at 12:15PM EDT by NWS Wilmington OH
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Central Logan County in west central Ohio...

* WHEN...Until 1215 PM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 909 AM EDT, local law enforcement reported flooding in the
warned area.  Between 3 and 4.5 inches of rain have fallen.
Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.5 inches are possible.
- Some locations that may experience flooding include...
Bellefontaine, West Liberty, Russells Point, Lakeview,
Huntsville, Valley Hi, Zanesfield, Mcmorran, New Jerusalem,
Pickrelltown, Lewistown, East Liberty and Middleburg.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

To report flooding, go to our website at weather.gov/iln and submit
your report via social media, when you can do so safely.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 4 at 8:09PM CDT until September 6 at 10:36AM CDT by NWS Lake Charles LA
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Neches River at Neches River Saltwater Barrier affecting Jefferson,
Hardin, Jasper and Orange Counties.

Village Creek Near Kountze affecting Hardin County.

...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...

Pine Island Bayou Near Sour Lake affecting Jefferson and Hardin
Counties.

For the Neches River...including Town Bluff, Evadale, Neches River
Saltwater Barrier...Minor flooding is forecast.
For the Village Creek...including Kountze...Moderate flooding is
forecast.
For the Pine Island Bayou...including Sour Lake...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...Village Creek near Kountze.

* WHEN...Until Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 21.9 feet, At this level, water will be flowing over
the Highway 418 bridge.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM CDT Friday the stage was 21.9 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 12.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM CDT Friday was 22.4 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage late
tomorrow evening and continue falling to 5.9 feet Wednesday
evening.
- Flood stage is 17.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 21.8
feet on 02/12/1966.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Saturday morning at 815 AM CDT.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 5 at 5:55AM EDT until September 5 at 9:30AM EDT by NWS Wilmington OH
properties.description:
FFWILN

The National Weather Service in Wilmington has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Central Logan County in west central Ohio...

* Until 930 AM EDT.

* At 555 AM EDT, local law enforcement reported flash flooding across
the warned area. Between 3.5 and 4 inches of rain have fallen.
Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch are possible.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Law enforcement reported.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that may experience flash flooding include...
Bellefontaine, West Liberty, Russells Point, Lakeview, Huntsville,
Valley Hi, Zanesfield, Mcmorran, New Jerusalem, Pickrelltown,
Lewistown, East Liberty and Middleburg.

At 5:30 AM, local law enforcement reported high water over multiple
areas near and around Bellefontaine.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

To report flash flooding, go to our website at weather.gov/iln and
submit your report via social media, when you can do so safely.
